title: Graceful Fidelity Staircase and Degradation Modes
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines the "graceful fidelity staircase": a deliberate, observable sequence of degradation steps the serving runtime may take when capacity, latency, or cost constraints demand reduced resource usage or model fidelity. The staircase is intended to preserve availability and SLOs while minimizing user-visible quality regressions.

Goals
- Provide a single, auditable decision model for runtime-initiated fidelity changes.
- Make each degradation step reversible and safely testable in canaries.
- Tie telemetry signals and SLO thresholds to explicit rollback and escalation actions.
- Standardize operator runbooks and automation hooks for fidelity-layer transitions.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: hosted, dedicated, and private runtime deployments managed by Redwood inference runtime components (inference-router, batch-coordinator, kernel-proxy, kv-cache-daemon).
- Non-goal: this doc does not prescribe model-specific prompt transforms or application-level fallbacks (those belong to application owners).

Fidelity layers (catalog)

The runtime uses discrete layers (L0..L4) ordered from highest fidelity (L0) to lowest (L4). Each layer is described with expected quality impact, components affected, SLO target adjustment, and typical triggers.

| Layer | Short name | Effect on quality | Components impacted | Typical trigger | Estimated cost delta |
|-------|------------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| L0 | Full fidelity | No change in model output or decoding | Serving runtime: normal routing, full KV cache, quantization disabled | Healthy cluster, nominal load | 0% |
| L1 | Cache-prefill | Slightly faster responses for repeated prefixes; minimal quality change | kv-cache-daemon more aggressively serves prefixes; prefix prefetch enabled | Temporary tail-latency spikes | -5% |
| L2 | Batching+subscription | Minor increase in p50 latency and slight beam diversity loss | batch-coordinator increases target batch size; elastic batching active | Moderate sustained load, cost optimization window | -12% |
| L3 | Quantized runtime | Small quality regressions for some prompts; large cost savings | kernel-proxy switches to 4/8-bit kernels, evap pruning of KV | Cost-driven or capacity-constrained (70%+ GPU utilization) | -35% |
| L4 | Model-variant fallback | Noticeable fidelity change (smaller model variant) | inference-router routes to smaller variants or distilled models | Emergency capacity shortages or region outage | -60% |

Operational rules and decision graph

- The runtime evaluates the decision graph every 15s. Inputs: cluster utilization (GPU/CPU/mem), tail latency (p99), error rate, reserve capacity fraction, and cost budget signal.
- Hard SLO breaches (p99 > SLO*1.5 for >2m) trigger immediate protective steps: stop accepting new long-context requests and escalate to oncall.
- Soft pressure (sustained util > 65% for 10m) enters the staircase starting at L1 and progresses no more than one layer per 5m unless an emergency threshold is crossed.
- Rollback policy: a layer transition is reversed if KPIs (p99, error rate, avg tokens/sec) return to within safe margins for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (3x15s).

Mapping to runtime components (concrete)

- inference-router: implements routing rules and model-variant switching. Config keys: router.fidelity_stepback.enabled, router.max_fallback_percent.
- batch-coordinator: controls target_batch_size and dynamic_batch_window. Config keys: batch.target_size_hint, batch.max_latency_ms.
- kernel-proxy: holds kernel selection table and quantization profiles. Config keys: kernel.q_profile, kernel.fallback_sequence.
- kv-cache-daemon: controls prefix caching TTL and prefetch heuristics. Config keys: kv.prefix_ttl_ms, kv.prefetch_enabled.

Example config fragment (YAML)

fidelity_staircase:
  evaluation_interval_s: 15
  max_progress_per_window: 1
  layers:
    - { name: L1, action: kv.prefetch:true, priority: 10 }
    - { name: L2, action: batch.target_size_hint:32, priority: 20 }
    - { name: L3, action: kernel.q_profile:4bit, priority: 30 }
    - { name: L4, action: router.model_variant:compact-v2, priority: 40 }

Note: YAML above is a human-readable excerpt. The runtime operator objects accept the same keys under runtime.feature_flags.fidelity_staircase in the configuration API.

SLOs, thresholds and concrete numeric examples

- Global request SLO (example): p99_gen_latency <= 750ms, availability >= 99.95%.
- Emergency thresholds (example): p99_gen_latency > 2250ms for 2 minutes => escalate and advance staircase by 2 layers (skip L1).
- Cost window trigger: projected token-cost > budget_weekly * 1.12 => evaluate L3/L4 if utilization > 70%.

Escalation and human-in-the-loop steps

1) Automated action: runtime advances staircase layer (or applies targeted action). All changes are annotated in the decision-trace log with correlation ID and owner (automation).
2) Pager: if p99 remains > SLO*1.2 after 3 minutes, send page to inference-oncall with tag "fidelity-change".
3) Oncall procedure: follow the Runtime Fidelity Triage (see Runbook section). If human rollback is required, use the operator CLI: redwood-runtime fidelity rollback --correlation-id <id>.

Runbook: Runtime Fidelity Triage (for oncall)

1. Observe: open /dashboards/runtime/fidelity-overview, filter by model and region. Confirm the active layer and recent layer transitions.
2. Verify signals: GPUs (utilization), host memory, p99, error rate, KV hit ratio.
3. If layer was automated and KPIs improved: monitor for 15 minutes and allow automatic rollback.
4. If KPIs worsen or error rate increases > 3% absolute after a layer transition: immediately roll back one layer and page the runtime-owner.
5. If rollback fails or cannot restore SLOs: trigger incident and escalate to platform-incident channel.

Example CLI snippets

# show current fidelity status
redwood-runtime status --model my-chat --region us-west-2 --fields fidelity,correlation_id

# force rollback
redwood-runtime fidelity rollback --correlation-id 2026-06-10-abc123 --reason "rollback test"

# simulate L3 in canary
redwood-runtime canary create --target cluster:canary-usw --override kernel.q_profile=4bit --duration 30m

Telemetry, alerts and annotation conventions

- Decision-trace: every automated fidelity decision emits a decision-trace event (trace_id: string) with fields: from_layer, to_layer, reason, metrics_snapshot, triggered_by (auto/manual).
- Alert: fidelity-layer-progression-excessive fires when more than 3 layer changes happen within 10 minutes for the same model/region. Severity: P2.
- Dashboards: fidelity_overview (per-tenant), fidelity_latency_heatmap (cross model).

Playbook for reproducing and validating quality impact

1) Record baseline: capture 1000 representative requests from production (anonymized) using request-proxy replay.
2) Run A/B replay: replay corpus to L0 and L3 in the sandbox runtime and collect response diffs.
3) Metrics to compute: token-wise similarity (BLEU/ROUGE not ideal for chat; use embedding-similarity with cosine threshold), function-call fidelity, hallucination rate on a curated prompt set.
4) Quality gate: if embedding-similarity mean < 0.92 or hallucination increase > 1.5x, mark L3 as requiring additional tuning (quant profile or reduced batch size).

Safety and rollout checklist (pre-canary)

- Add unit tests for decision-graph transitions (simulate triggers).
- Create traffic mirroring rule for canary.
- Ensure canary cluster has at least 2x expected memory headroom for quantized kernels.
- Create evaluation prompt set and automated comparator job.

Appendix: short glossary

- Fidelity staircase: ordered set of runtime degradation actions applied to reduce resource usage or preserve availability.
- Decision-trace: structured event emitted for every automated fidelity decision.

Appendix: minimal experiment matrix (CSV-ready)
